body.x: [Las Vegas, USA = AVING News] At CES 2026 in Las Vegas, one technology stopped industry professionals in their tracks—one that began with a deceptively simple question:
“Is it possible to remove only the water mixed inside oil using a filter?”
EcoRenew (CEO Duckhyun Choi) presented a clear and confident answer: a superhydrophobic filter that blocks water while selectively allowing oil to pass through.

At CES 2026, EcoRenew unveiled its superhydrophobic nano-coated Renuva-Oil (RO) filter as the centerpiece of its exhibition. While conventional oil–water separation technologies focus on removing oil from water, the Renuva-Oil filter takes the opposite approach—removing microscopic, emulsified water from within oil itself. This was long considered virtually impossible within the industry.

body.cap: The superhydrophobic Renuva-Oil filter unveiled by EcoRenew at CES 2026. It represents a world-first nano-coating concept that selectively passes oil while blocking water. | Photo – AVING News

body.x: “Hydrophobic Alone Is Not Enough” — Engineering Selectivity into the Filter

CEO Duckhyun Choi explained on-site, “Most hydrophobic filters end up blocking both water and oil. What EcoRenew achieved was precise control over nano-coating selectivity, allowing oil to flow smoothly while preventing water from passing through.”

With this single filter, traditional waste oil purification processes—previously dependent on high temperature, high pressure, and massive energy input—can be transformed into a low-temperature, low-pressure filtration process. Purification is possible without heating beyond 60°C, significantly reducing both energy consumption and carbon emissions.
"Field-Proven Technology… First Commercial Delivery Completed in Late December"

EcoRenew’s confidence in its technology has already translated into tangible results. In late December 2025, the company delivered its first Renuva-Oil–based purification system to a domestic metal forging company, officially moving beyond proof-of-concept and into commercial deployment.

In metal processing operations, lubricating oil and coolant are used simultaneously, inevitably generating waste oil over time. Traditionally, this waste oil had to be shipped to external refiners or discarded after weeks-long processing. With EcoRenew’s system, companies can now perform continuous on-site purification within just 2–3 hours, enabling stable reuse of several tons of lubricating oil per month.

body.cap: EcoRenew’s Renuva filter lineup. The upper cartridge is the superhydrophobic Renuva-Oil, while the lower is the superhydrophilic Renuva-Water. By simply replacing the filter, the same system can switch between oil and water purification. | Photo – AVING News

body.x: "Modular Architecture: Scaling Capacity Up to 100×"

Renuva-Oil is integrated into EcoRenew’s continuous purification system, RenewFlow-Oil (RFO). Its most notable feature is a multi-housing modular design. By increasing filter length and quantity, processing capacity can be expanded by 10 times—or even up to 100 times.

When superhydrophilic filters are installed instead, the same housing transforms into RenewFlow-Water, an industrial water purification system. In other words, a simple filter swap determines whether the system purifies oil or water.
“Equal to or Better Than Virgin Oil” — Quality Validation Achieved

The quality of the regenerated oil was another critical benchmark. EcoRenew has secured evaluations confirming reusability through analysis frameworks aligned with the Korea Petroleum Quality & Distribution Authority, as well as independent professional testing institutions. Formal certification procedures are currently underway, with completion targeted for the first half of the year.

“Compared to using virgin oil, reusing purified oil can reduce carbon dioxide emissions by up to 80%,” said Choi. “This technology simultaneously addresses two challenges: resource circulation and carbon reduction.”

body.cap: A display panel illustrating the structure and operating principle of RenewFlow-Oil (RFO). The superhydrophobic filter selectively allows oil to pass while separating water and solid contaminants. | Photo – AVING News

body.x: "From POSCO to Chemicals — Demand Is Already Wide Open"

EcoRenew’s target market is clearly defined: any industrial site that uses lubricating oil, including metal processing, steelmaking, machinery, chemicals, and cosmetics manufacturing. Looking ahead, the company also envisions applications in Middle Eastern crude oil extraction, where water injection is used to lift oil—resulting in moisture-laden crude that requires downstream dehydration.
“As a starting point, this is just the beginning,” Choi remarked. “But a filter that blocks water and passes only oil is a technology that fundamentally reshapes industrial processes.”
With CES 2026 as its launchpad, EcoRenew is accelerating a paradigm shift in waste oil purification—from thermal processing to selective filtration.
The technology has already been proven on-site.
Now, only one question remains: Which company will be the first to adopt it at scale?
